reviews.comment: Incredible class, the prof was always nice and super knowledgeable, nothing more to say. You have to take this course or you're not living life.
This is the best class if you want to graduate and get a job. The problems are really fun.
amazing. perfect. 430 is the best class to take ever.
Kind of boring and fast paced course. Without TAs help, it is hard.

Lectures were fine, not well attended. Don't really need them to get an A. The class is just a bunch competitive programming problems. Extra credit opportunities. Miserable experience but not because of Keyser. He was fine. If you're not already good at competitive programming, this class will not be fun.

Dr. Keyser is so passionate it just makes me want to do work. Which you will have to do a lot of in this class, but will pay off. TAs are super helpful though, both for the problems during the week as well as the problem sets. The class moves pretty fast, so if you haven't done any sort of leetcode/competitive programming it might not be for you.

Labs are mandatory and if you do less than half of the base problem for any one week you cannot get an A, but generally super reasonable class and probably my favorite. If competitive programming/leetcode is one of your most disliked topics then this class may not be for you, it will be a challenge either way.
Favorite class I've taken. If you can get 100% of the problems before spring break, then the rest of the class shouldn't be to bad. You learn a lot and the TA's are very useful.
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Keyser is a friendly and fair prof, and I found the class quite fun.  To get an A, you either have to (a) already have skills in competitive programming or (b) put in extra time solving homework problems.  Notably though, the professor and TAs are (for the most part) accessible outside of class / office hours so getting help is simple when needed
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lectures are not worth going to in my opinion, but time management is all you need for this class. The TAs are usually great and your grade is just dependent on how many problems you solve in the class so start early in the week and do as many as you can as soon as you can. This class was the most time consuming class I've ever taken

Get a head start and do the extra credit problems early in the semester! That's the cheat code for this class and I promise you it will help. Well spoken, respected, and understanding but also maintains the integrity of the class. Put the work in and it will pay off in dividends (in more ways than one) during tech interviews!

You attend lab on fridays and weekly problem sets due every week. A very useful class that teaches you how to analyze problems and determine correct and efficient algorithms to use. Keyser is a great prof who explains the algorithms extremely well and cares about students. Be ready to work a lot if you perform poorly on the labs and problem sets.

You will learn a lot about algorithms and how to apply them to various situations. Also you'll learn how to implement ideas into solutions. It's pretty easy to make an A if you stay on top of your coursework as there are no exams and everything can be upsolved for half credit. You only need a certain amount solved by the end.

Class graded based off the 14 or so class meetings where you have to answer a 4 question quiz based off what was discussed during the lecture. Then one completion grade exam at the end. Class ends at midterm. Keyser is pretty chill and seems like a good guy. If you fail/miss attendance grades you can make them up by doing a 1-page essay on a topic.

Caring and knowledgeable guy, would definitely take him for any other classes he teaches. This class only lasted half the semester. Grade was determined by quizzes at the end of each lecture to make sure you were paying attention, but any of them could be made up with a short essay on a research topic which he gave suggestions for.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Keyser is one of my favorite professors I have taken. You can genuinely tell he cares about his students and wants them to learn, and that he is passionate about the course. CSCE 430 is an easy A if you are dedicated to doing the HW's and are decent at the labs (which are the only grades) - but note it is time consuming. Took in Spring 2020
